newsitem.title: USA: Snow and ice block highways in U.S. Southwest.
newsitem.headline: Snow and ice block highways in U.S. Southwest.

text.p: Heavy snow storms and ice caused traffic chaos in the usually sunny U.S. Southwest with at least three people dying in weather-related accidents, police said Tuesday.

Tucson, Ariz. had its first snow showers in five years and the mountains around Albuquerque, N.M., were blanketed with up to three feet of snow. Interstate 10 was closed until midday in southern Arizona and all the way through New Mexico to the border with Texas.
Interstate 25, which runs north-south through New Mexico, was also closed for most of Tuesday morning and other smaller roads remained closed in the afternoon.
In western Texas, three people were killed in accidents caused by up to six inches of snow, frozen rain and 50 mph winds in and around the border city of El Paso.
"It is icy, slushy, messy and very slick. We do not recommend travelling," a spokesman with the Department of Public Safety in El Paso said on Tuesday afternoon.
The storms, which meteorologists said may have been the worst to hit the region in a decade, swept through on Monday and even dropped some light snow as far east as Dallas.

Police said slick conditions caused hundreds of road accidents, although most of them were little more than fender-benders. Experts said more snow might fall across the area late Tuesday but that the worst of the storms had passed.
"The worst of it is probably over," said Jim Reynolds, a meteorologist with the National Weather Service in southern New Mexico. "The upper level system has headed south to northern Mexico."
